name: MK-677
summary: An experimental oral drug that mimics the hormone ghrelin to raise growth hormone and IGF-1, taken for muscle, sleep and recovery; FDA bars compounding over heart-failure risk.
what_it_is: MK-677, or ibutamoren, is an experimental drug taken by mouth that mimics ghrelin, a natural hormone that triggers growth hormone release. In trials it raised growth hormone and IGF-1 in older adults to levels typical of young adults. It was studied in the 1990s and 2000s for age-related muscle loss and recovery after hip fracture.

evidence.why: Randomized trials in older adults show it raises growth hormone, IGF-1 and lean mass but not strength or function, sleep data come from two tiny studies, and a hip-fracture trial was stopped early over heart failure.

status_us.label: FDA Category 2: pharmacies may not compound it
status_us.note: FDA lists ibutamoren mesylate in Category 2 for both compounding pharmacies (since September 2023) and outsourcing facilities (since December 2022), citing a risk of congestive heart failure, and it remained there on FDA's 2025 and 2026 lists. WADA bans ibutamoren (MK-677) in sport.

benefits.claim: Raised growth hormone and IGF-1 to young-adult levels over 12 months in a randomized trial of 65 healthy adults aged 60 to 81
Increased lean (fat-free) mass by about 1 kg versus a small loss on placebo, without gains in strength or function
Faster walking (gait speed) but no improvement in most other function measures in 123 older adults recovering from hip fracture
More deep (stage IV) and REM sleep in short studies of 8 young and 6 older adults

risks.risk: Congestive heart failure: a hip-fracture trial in older adults was stopped early over a heart-failure safety signal, which FDA cites as a significant safety risk
Higher fasting blood sugar and lower insulin sensitivity over a year in older adults
Increased appetite (usually fading within a few months), mild temporary leg swelling and muscle pain, the most frequent side effects in a 2-year trial
Weight gain of about 2.7 kg over a year (vs 0.8 kg on placebo), including more fat on the arms and legs

avoid_if: Heart failure or other heart disease (heart-failure safety signal in older adults)
Diabetes or prediabetes (it raises fasting glucose and lowers insulin sensitivity)
Current or past cancer, unless a clinician advises otherwise (it raises IGF-1, a growth signal)
interactions: Diabetes medicines: it raises fasting glucose and lowers insulin sensitivity, which can work against glucose control

before: General health check with a clinician, including fasting glucose
labs.why: No evidence-based monitoring exists for MK-677; trials found raised IGF-1, higher fasting glucose and a heart-failure signal.

studies.title: Effects of an oral ghrelin mimetic on body composition and clinical outcomes in healthy older adults: A randomized trial
studies.finding: Over 12 months, MK-677 raised growth hormone and IGF-1 to young-adult levels and increased fat-free mass by about 1 kg versus a small loss with placebo, without changes in strength or function. Fasting glucose rose and insulin sensitivity fell.

studies.title: MK-0677 (ibutamoren mesylate) for the treatment of patients recovering from hip fracture: A multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled phase IIb study
studies.people: 123 older adults recovering from hip fracture
studies.finding: Over 24 weeks, IGF-1 rose and gait speed improved, but most function measures did not. The trial was stopped early over a heart-failure safety signal, and the authors judged its safety profile unfavorable.

studies.title: Prolonged oral treatment with MK-677, a novel growth hormone secretagogue, improves sleep quality in man
studies.people: 8 adults aged 18 to 30 and 6 aged 65 to 71
studies.finding: Over 1 to 2 weeks, deep sleep rose by about half and REM sleep by more than a fifth versus placebo in young adults; REM sleep rose by nearly half in older adults, whose part may not have been blinded.

ask_your_clinician: Given FDA's heart-failure concern, should I avoid it?
How would it affect my blood sugar, and should we check glucose or HbA1c?
If my goal is strength, which approaches improve it, since MK-677 added lean mass but not strength?

notes_for_editor: FDA's Category 2 entry (503A since September 29, 2023; 503B since December 29, 2022) cites the hip-fracture trial's heart-failure signal; the number of heart-failure cases was not in the abstract we read. The 2008 trial was read on a University of Kentucky repository page and the 2011 trial on a Tel Aviv University repository page, because PubMed records were not reachable. 'Experimental drug' rests on the trial literature; we did not find an approval anywhere. The cancer caution is an inference from its IGF-1 effect. The 2008 Alzheimer's disease trial was not reviewed within the search budget. Frequency labels for appetite, swelling and muscle pain reflect the trial calling them the most common side effects; exact rates were not in the abstract. Cortisol also rose modestly in the 2008 trial (not listed above).
